content: Viburnum tinus, also known as Laurustinus, Laurustinus Viburnum, or Laurestine, is a species of flowering plant belonging to the genus Viburnum. It is native to the Mediterranean region and Macaronesia. The name Laurus refers to the resemblance of its leaves to those of the bay laurel, while tinus translates to tenth born. This plant is typically a shrub, though it can occasionally grow into a small tree, reaching heights of 2 to 7 meters. It has a dense, rounded crown. The leaves are evergreen, persisting for 2 to 3 years, and are arranged in opposite pairs. They measure 4 to 10 cm in length and 2 to 4 cm in width, with smooth, entire margins. The flowers of Viburnum tinus are white and are produced in dense, rounded clusters (cymes) that measure 5 to 10 cm in diameter. These flowers bloom during the winter season. The fruit is a dark blue-black drupe, measuring 5 to 7 mm in length. There are three recognized subspecies of Viburnum tinus: 1. Viburnum tinus subsp. tinus: Found in the Mediterranean region. 2. Viburnum tinus subsp. rigidum (synonym: Viburnum rigidum): Native to the Canary Islands. 3. Viburnum tinus subsp. subcordatum: Found in the Azores. Cultivation and Uses Viburnum tinus is a widely cultivated evergreen shrub, valued for its ability to flower during the winter months. It is particularly popular in regions with mild winters. It is grown extensively in Western Europe, as far north as Britain, and in North America, reaching as far north as western British Columbia.
